claim: A guy asks on social media how to stay on course. He always has a good start and good intention but keeps falling back into old habits (watching pornography, eating trash food, stopping exercise). He wants to be the best version of himself, but seems to always fall back to things that drag him down further, and his mental health doesn't fare well then
A lot of guys possibly struggle with always falling back into old habits after a good start and good intention, now, have before or will: it is a very human thing
Small things stack: the first thing to understand, it seems, is that most areas of life, including self-care and self-empowerment, are not big events but the stacking of a lot of small things
We don't reach a high vibration (fit, mentally and sexually well) or sink into a low one and old unproductive habits through one or two big events
Most areas of life being not big events but the stacking of a lot of small things is actually good
From a low place, where we want to be often seems so far away, a big task, but it's not really as big as it seems: the task is a little win, then another, then another
Little wins are achievable and also feel within reach

An example of little wins: a hundred pounds overweight, losing a hundred pounds seems really big, and in some ways it is, but making this next meal healthier is much more doable, and seems it, so you're more likely to follow through

section: How to get back on track
claim: Off course, first and foremost get small wins
Tracking: for good starts followed by failing, the big thing found personally to make a world of difference
Tracking keeps you accountable and lets you know sooner when you fall off
After working out every day or six days a week for a couple of weeks, if habits just live in your head, one missed day becomes two, four, six, two weeks: "man, I haven't worked out in two weeks"
Tracking, you notice a missed day immediately
Do something three or four days in a row and that's a new habit, so three or four days without training is a new habit of not training, a new path
The act of tracking itself keeps you on the path
In tracking, checking off the day's task is an important psychological feedback loop, a satisfaction that makes doing it tomorrow that much more likely
Tracking shows how consistent you are, and consistency is what matters
Off and on gets us nowhere, back in the same place
Be consistent enough that a habit shifts your identity
name: Identity

claim: For working out to stay with you for years, for decades, it must become part of who you are, with no background identity saying "I'm working out right now, but it's kind of not really who I am"
name: Identity

claim: Done consistently enough, working out becomes just who you are, more ingrained the longer it lasts
name: Identity

claim: Once overweight, out of shape, struggling with porn, excessive ejaculation and so many things discussed here, and an alcoholic ("lots there to unpack another day"). So many of those things completely changed, to the point where they will never go back: years and years of training essentially every day, minus occasional rest days, because the identity shifted
name: Identity

claim: The only way to get consistent is tracking
Personally, no one worked with or heard from in the last few years has yet made significant changes in areas such as porn, exercise and eating trash food without some kind of tracking of key habits
Over and over, when guys start one-on-one and implement tracking, they improve: not all the way at once, not perfectly, with steps back, but "what gets tracked gets improved"
Changing porn, exercise and eating trash all at once is not going to go well, or maybe goes well for a period and then you fall off
Start small: pick a smaller number of things and be "ruthlessly consistent"
Once one, two or three small things are ingrained, part of your identity, add another, then another, slowly over time
Thinking so many things need to change overwhelms you, a lot of times sending you further down the low-vibration path
Dial back the mental approach that so many things need to change: one or two things, ruthlessly consistent, tracked every day

Suggested for a listener who keeps falling back into old habits, every single day: a cold shower and some kind of physical training, even five minutes to start, without worrying about changing everything else
For others the habits to start with may not be a cold shower and physical training: look at your situation and pick one or two small empowering habits
For tracking, find one of the many habit-tracking apps that works for you (one is used personally with clients and really liked), or use sticky notes or a dry-erase board
How you track habits doesn't really matter; tracking does
Not exercising now, don't make your change an hour a day: from nothing to an hour every single day, consistently, isn't realistic, "It's not gonna happen"
Not exercising now, dial your change back to something small and achievable
A cold shower every morning, kind of another discussion: so many reasons it is such a powerful habit, the biggest being mental strength and discipline
Men who start their day with a cold shower make different, more powerful choices the rest of the day, "You just will"
Physiological benefits and other reasons aside, the number one reason a cold shower every morning is recommended is that you will be more disciplined

After a couple of weeks, a few weeks, of the cold shower and the five or maybe 10-minute workout every day, increase or add: maybe the workout from 10 to 20 minutes, then nutrition, one small food choice at a time, then different choices about porn and your sexual health

"I promise": with small building blocks, one small win at a time, and your tracking system as a daily habit, you will improve and lock some things into your identity, never going back, a beautiful place, experienced personally and seen in so many guys

section: How to get back on track
claim: Even if staying on course has been up and down and never stuck, whether you think you can or not, "you absolutely can do it"
Track every day, whether it gets done or not
When your tracking system shows the next morning that something didn't get done, you immediately get back on the path, toward some permanent changes that become part of who you are
